title: How you fight with someone you love
dek: Not the tidy version you'd tell a therapist. Twelve questions about the last real argument and what you actually do in the middle of it.

questions.prompt: It starts over something small. Your first move:

options.label: Say the thing you'll have to apologise for
Bring up a very specific previous incident
Try to solve it within ninety seconds

questions.prompt: The thing you can't help doing:

options.label: Cry, and hate that you're crying
Make a joke at the worst possible moment
Need to leave the room immediately
Ask what outcome they actually want

questions.prompt: Your worst version of yourself shows up as:

options.label: Everything at once, in the wrong order

questions.prompt: The evidence you bring to the argument:

options.label: A fix, offered before they've finished the sentence
A very good reason to be somewhere else
Someone says something too loud and it's over
You clean the kitchen and it's somehow resolved
A joke lands and you both take the exit
A ten-minute break, then an actual conversation

questions.prompt: What you say afterwards that you don't mean:

options.label: A bit about how dramatic you both were

questions.prompt: The real feeling underneath, most often:

options.label: I said too much and I can't take it back
I need to not be in this room

questions.prompt: Rank what you actually want out of a fight.
questions.helper: Not what you say you want. The order gives it away.

questions.prompt: I get loud before I get clear.
Leaving the room is a valid argument technique.
Pick the room where the argument actually happens.

options.label: The kitchen at 1am
options.alt: A kitchen lit by one lamp at night

options.label: The car, engine off
options.alt: The inside of a car at night

options.label: Two mugs gone cold
options.alt: Two coffee mugs on a table

results.name: The Silence
results.blurb: You don't shout, you disappear politely. The conversation stops, the flat goes quiet, and you wait for them to come and find you. You're not being cruel — you genuinely need time to assemble the sentence. It just takes you until Thursday.
results.watchOut: Silence reads as punishment even when it isn't. Say when you'll come back.

results.name: The Volcano
results.blurb: It comes out all at once and it's over in ninety seconds, and you're genuinely surprised anyone's still upset. The volume isn't hatred, it's velocity. You'd just like everyone to know that you're fine now, which is not how feelings work for other people.
strengths: Says it instead of storing it
results.watchOut: Your ninety seconds lands in someone else's week. Lower the volume, keep the point.

results.name: The Historian
results.blurb: You remember the exact wording, the date and what you were wearing, and you bring it out with the calm of a prosecutor. You're not being petty — you're proving you're not imagining the pattern. The other person only hears the archive.
results.watchOut: One current thing at a time. The archive can wait for a calmer day.

results.name: The Fixer
results.blurb: The second something hurts, you're already three steps into a solution. It comes from love and it lands as dismissal. You'll offer a plan before they've finished their sentence, then feel rejected when the plan isn't the thing they wanted.
results.watchOut: Ask 'do you want help or do you want company?' before offering either.

results.name: The Crier
results.blurb: Your face starts before your argument does, and then you're apologising for crying instead of finishing the point. The feeling is real and enormous and completely unhelpful mid-sentence. You leave arguments having never said the actual thing.
results.watchOut: Write the point down. You don't have to deliver it perfectly to say it.

results.name: The Comedian
results.blurb: You can make anyone laugh, including in the middle of the worst conversation of the year. It's a genuine gift and it's also how you leave the room without moving. The joke buys you ten seconds and costs you the chance to be taken seriously.
results.watchOut: Let one serious sentence land without a follow-up joke. It'll survive.

results.name: The Runner
results.blurb: The walls close in and you're out — a walk, a drive, a sudden errand. It's not that you don't care; it's that you can't think in that room. The problem is you always come back to a person who's been sitting alone with the thing you left.
strengths: Protects the conversation from the worst version of you
results.watchOut: Say when you're returning. Disappearing isn't the same as pausing.

results.name: The Negotiator
results.tagline: Wants the rule, not the win
results.blurb: You'd rather agree a process than be right, which makes you excellent in a crisis and slightly exhausting in a feeling. You've suggested a ten-minute cooling-off period during an argument about a birthday. It works. It also makes people want to shake you.
results.watchOut: Some moments don't need a process, they need you to just be upset with them.
